en.headline: Police receive over 100 reports of credit card charges linked to iPhone Duo pre-orders
en.dek: Complaints of duplicate or unauthorised transactions began after Apple opened online pre-orders at 8pm on Friday, with sums running into the millions of dollars.
body: Hong Kong police have received more than 100 reports concerning credit card transactions related to pre-orders of Apple’s foldable iPhone Duo, according to sources familiar with the matter.

Apple began accepting online pre-orders at 8pm on Friday. Within hours, users reported receiving payment alerts for charges they said were duplicate or unauthorised. Some who successfully ordered the device said the same amount was billed multiple times, while others claimed their pre-orders failed yet their cards were still charged. A number of people said they had not attempted to order at all.

Most reports involved cards issued by HSBC. One account was said to have been charged about HK$175,000 across several transactions. Sources indicated the overall sums involved were at least several million dollars and still rising. HSBC has said some repeated authorisations stemmed from operational issues during the busy period and that affected transactions would be cancelled.

Apple has said it reviews every iPhone Duo order before processing and is working to identify and cancel fraudulent ones before shipment. The pattern is similar to reports that followed the launch of the iPhone 18 Pro models last month. Police are continuing their enquiries.

zh.headline: 警方接獲逾百宗iPhone Duo預購信用卡扣款舉報
zh.dek: 蘋果周五晚八時開放摺疊式手機預購後，市民紛紛反映重複或未經授權交易，涉及金額達數百萬元。
body: 據消息人士透露，香港警方已接獲超過一百宗與蘋果摺疊式手機iPhone Duo預購相關的信用卡交易舉報。
蘋果於周五晚上八時開始接受網上預購。隨後數小時內，有用戶收到付款通知，指交易屬重複或未經授權。部分成功下單者稱同一金額被多次扣款，亦有人表示預購失敗但仍被扣款，另有市民聲稱根本沒有嘗試訂購。
大部分舉報涉及匯豐銀行發出的信用卡。其中一個戶口據稱被多次扣款合共約十七萬五千元。消息指整體涉及金額至少數百萬元，仍在上升。匯豐表示，部分重複授權源於繁忙時段的操作問題，相關交易將會取消。
蘋果表示會在處理前審核每一宗iPhone Duo訂單，並正識別及取消欺詐訂單，以免出貨。情況與上月iPhone 18 Pro系列開售後出現的舉報相似。警方仍在調查。
